theme.description: The design-system selection iarch-theme renders from, added in Part 2. It sits alongside the coarse Part-1 'preset' master switch and the 'effects' toggles rather than replacing them: 'colour_preset' names one of the palettes in data/design/presets/ (validated at runtime against that directory, so the list stays open), and 'intensity' names one of the four the tokens define. configstore.load merges the repository default under a user's file, so a settings.json written before this block existed still resolves a theme. iarch-theme apply writes both keys back here; reconciling them with the coarse 'preset'/'effects' switches is Part 4 settings-app work.

animation.description: The motion state iarch-anim renders from, added in Part 3. It is deliberately separate from 'theme': a theme is a look (colour preset plus intensity) and this is how that look moves, so a person can be on frosted glass and bouncy motion, or on the Performance intensity — which pairs with the 'off' preset — without either choice overwriting the other. 'preset' names a file in data/design/animations/, 'speed' is the global multiplier where a number above 1 is FASTER because it divides every duration, 'reduce_motion' forces the minimal preset with every duration capped, and 'event_overrides' maps an animation leaf to whether the user turned it on or off on top of whatever the preset declares. The overrides are keyed by leaf name, which is an open set the compositor defines rather than one this schema can enumerate, so the values are constrained to booleans here and the names are checked against data/design/animations.json at render time. Not in the top-level 'required' list on purpose: configstore.load merges these defaults under a settings.json written before this block existed, so an older user file still resolves and still validates. The 0.5 and 2.0 bounds duplicate tokens.json motion.animation.speed_multiplier because a schema cannot read another file; tests/test_animation_presets.py asserts the two agree.
